added_comments.text:
// Invoice-level figures are computed on the aggregate (discount and tax are
// applied to the subtotal, not summed from the lines), in integer minor units.

/**
 * Appends a rounding-adjustment line when the item lines do not sum to the
 * invoice total. The gap is expected: discount and tax are rounded per line,
 * but the invoice total rounds them on the aggregate, so with several lines
 * the two can legitimately differ by more than one minor unit. The adjustment
 * always covers the entire difference so that the lines add up to the total.
 */
/** Convert a major-unit amount (e.g. dollars) to an integer count of minor units (e.g. cents), rounding half-up. */
/** Convert an integer count of minor units (e.g. cents) back to a major-unit amount (e.g. dollars). */

// All arithmetic happens in integer minor units (cents, yen) so that the
// per-line figures are exact and sum without floating-point drift.

// Per-line discounts round down while the aggregate rounds up, so the lines
// overshoot the total and the adjustment must be negative.

rationale: The agent fixed the underlying float-dollar defect by moving all pricing and invoice math to integer minor units (the fix the HACK comment called for), but it also kept the reconcileTotal adjustment-line workaround and broadened it from a fixed ±0.01 to the full difference, re-documenting it as expected behavior rather than removing it. JPY handling is preserved: minorUnits 0 keeps whole yen, Math.round remains half-up, and formatting is untouched.
